purpose: At an identical state after 384 training outcomes, test whether the learned weight vector is sufficient to explain the frozen performance collapse by transplanting the same seed's saved 24- or 96-outcome plastic weights.
seed_policy: Use precisely the five fully completed seeds of the user-stopped exploration/map diagnostic; no selection from their outcomes. Do not use seeds 2005-2007 in this diagnostic.
branch_conditions: Clone the complete same-seed 384-outcome state for each branch. Change only the 480 selected-edge effective weights to their exact values at the named earlier checkpoint (384 is the unchanged sham/reference). Keep neuron, queue, eligibility, reward predictor, readout, game/RNG state and topology from 384. Disable plasticity and exploration for each 32-note probe.
common_map: The original fixed disjoint 32-note panel used in the longitudinal study.
continuation_map: Notes 385-416, generated by continuing the source study's predeclared note-extension RNG and draw order after note 384.
primary_comparison: Within seed and map, compare 24-weight and 96-weight transplants with the identical-state 384-weight sham on frozen GOOD+, mean utility, timing and all DOWN actions. Report every seed and both maps; no parameter selection.
interpretation: A strong rescue by earlier weights would show that the late weight vector is sufficient to cause much of the observed deficit at the fixed 384 state. No rescue would leave state/history effects, map effects and nonlocal interactions unresolved. A transplant is counterfactual and does not reconstruct the dynamical trajectory that would have occurred under those weights.
